## Direct Answer: How to Crack RPF SI & Constable in 45 Days

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> **Core Fact**: The decisive battleground in RPF recruitment is the **50-mark General Awareness (GA)** section, which carries over 41.6% of total marks in the 120-question Computer Based Test. Scoring 40+ in GA, combined with 30+ in Arithmetic and 32+ in Reasoning, guarantees a safe merit position to qualify for the Physical Efficiency Test (PET).

The Railway Protection Force (**RPF**), operating under the Ministry of Railways, offers premier armed law-enforcement careers in India. As an **RPF Sub-Inspector (Pay Level 6)** or **RPF Constable (Pay Level 3)**, recruits are responsible for railway security, passenger safety, and counter-sabotage operations across Indian Railways. With only 45 days remaining before the CBT examination, this fast-track revision guide focuses strictly on high-yield questions, formula shortcuts, and accuracy control under time pressure.

---

## RPF CBT Exam Pattern & Mark Distribution

The online examination is identical in structure for both SI and Constable, featuring 120 questions to be solved in 90 minutes with **1/3rd (0.33) marks penalty** for wrong answers:

| Subject Domain | Total Questions | Maximum Marks | Mark Weightage Graph | Target Attempts (Accuracy >95%) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **General Awareness (GA & Science)** | 50 Questions | 50 Marks | [BAR:41.7%:General Awareness] | 42 – 45 Questions (Target: 40+ Marks) |
| **Arithmetic (Mathematics)** | 35 Questions | 35 Marks | [BAR:29.2%:Arithmetic] | 30 – 33 Questions (Target: 30+ Marks) |
| **General Intelligence & Reasoning** | 35 Questions | 35 Marks | [BAR:29.2%:Reasoning] | 32 – 35 Questions (Target: 32+ Marks) |
| **Total Composite Benchmark** | **120 Questions** | **120 Marks** | **[BAR:100%:Total Composite Test]** | **Composite Target: 102+ Marks (90 Mins)** |

---

## High-Yield 50-Mark General Awareness Topic Breakdown

RPF General Awareness does not require deep UPSC-level theoretical essays; it tests high-frequency factual recall across six core segments:

| GA Segment | Typical Questions | High-Yield Topics to Revise First |
|---|---|---|
| **General Science (Physics/Chem/Bio)** | 14 – 16 Questions | Human Body Systems (Digestive, Circulatory), Vitamins & Deficiencies, Newton's Laws, Optics, Common Chemical Compounds (Bleaching Powder, Plaster of Paris). |
| **Indian Polity & Constitution** | 8 – 10 Questions | Fundamental Rights (Articles 14 to 32), Directive Principles, President Election & Emergency Powers, Parliament, Constitutional Amendments (42nd, 44th, 86th, 101st). |
| **Modern Indian History** | 6 – 8 Questions | Governor Generals & Viceroys, 1857 Revolt leaders, Indian National Congress sessions & presidents, Gandhian Movements (1920, 1930, 1942). |
| **Indian Geography** | 6 – 8 Questions | Major River Basins (Himalayan vs Peninsular), National Parks & Wildlife Sanctuaries, Mineral Belts, Mountain Peaks & Passes. |
| **Indian Railways Static GK** | 4 – 6 Questions | History of first train in India, Railway Zones and Headquarters, Vande Bharat train manufacturing (ICF Chennai), Dedicated Freight Corridors (DFC). |
| **Current Affairs & Sports** | 8 – 10 Questions | Last 8 months current affairs, Olympic/Asian Games medalists, National Sports Awards, Chief Justices, and Union Cabinet Portfolios. |

## 45-Day Fast-Track Revision Plan

### Sprint 1 (Days 1 to 15): Core Concept Review & Formula Drill
- **General Awareness**: Complete Indian Polity (Articles & Amendments) and Class 9/10 NCERT General Science highlights.
- **Arithmetic**: Revise all formulas for Percentage, Ratio, Simple & Compound Interest, and Speed-Time-Distance (Trains & Platforms).
- **Reasoning**: Practice 40 questions daily on coding-decoding, alphanumeric series, and syllogisms.
- **Physical Fitness Check**: Start morning jogs (1600m for males, 800m for females) 4 days a week to ensure you are ready when PET notifications are released.

### Sprint 2 (Days 16 to 30): Sectional Speed Drills & High-Frequency MCQs
- **General Awareness**: Complete Modern Indian History, River Systems, and last 6 months of national and sports current affairs.
- **Arithmetic**: Solve 30 mixed PYQ problems every morning within 35 minutes.
- **Reasoning**: Focus on seating arrangements, statement-conclusions, and missing number grids.
- **Testing**: Take 2 sectional tests every 3 days to eliminate calculation slowness.

### Sprint 3 (Days 31 to 45): Full Computer Simulations & Mistake Elimination
- **Daily Full Mock Test**: Take 1 full 90-minute computer-based mock test at the exact scheduled time of your exam shift.
- **Negative Marking Guardrails**: If you cannot eliminate at least two options through deduction, skip the question. Avoid blind guesses to preserve your raw score.
- **Mistake Analysis**: Dedicate 1.5 hours after each mock test to understand why you got questions wrong and revise the corresponding theory chapter.
- **Final 5 Days**: Stop taking new tests. Revise formula notebooks, railway facts, and static GK one-liners.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### Q1: What are the physical standards for RPF Sub-Inspector (SI)?
Male candidates (UR/OBC) must complete the 1600-meter run in 6 minutes 30 seconds, clear a 12-foot long jump, and achieve a 3-foot 9-inch high jump. Female candidates (UR/OBC) must complete the 800-meter run in 4 minutes, clear a 9-foot long jump, and achieve a 3-foot high jump.

### Q2: Is the RPF exam qualifying or merit-based?
The Computer Based Test (CBT) marks are 100% merit-based. Scores in the CBT determine your final merit ranking, while the Physical Efficiency Test (PET) and Physical Measurement Test (PMT) are qualifying in nature.

### Q3: Is there sectional cut-off in RPF SI or Constable?
No, there is no sectional cut-off in the RPF exam. However, candidates must secure an overall qualifying percentage (35% for UR/OBC and 30% for SC/ST), though actual competitive cut-offs are substantially higher (typically 85+ out of 120).

### Q4: How is normalization calculated in the RPF examination?
Since the exam is conducted across multiple shifts and days, raw scores are normalized using the standard Railway Recruitment Board percentile-based normalization formula to account for variation in shift difficulty levels.
